Wreath products of semigroups in universal algebraic
geometry and Plotkin‘s problem
A.N. Shevlyakov
August 7, 2020
Abstract
We prove that the wreath product C = A ≀B of a semigroup A with zero and
an inﬁnite cyclic semigroup B is qω-compact (logically Noetherian).
Our result
partially solves the Plotkin‘s problem about wreath products in [6].
1
Introduction
Our research is devoted to the studies in universal algebraic geometry. This direc-
tion was initiated in papers by B. Plotkin [7] and E. Daniyarova, A. Miasnikov,
V. Remeslennikov [2], and it deals with equations over various algebraic structures
(semigroups, groups, Lie algebras, etc.). In the current paper we study semigroup
equations, but the problem we solved comes from group theory.
In our paper we deal with wreath products. Wreath products plays a central
role in the studies of group varieties and extensions of groups. The deﬁnition of a
wreath product may be naturally given for semigroups, where wreath products have
important applications in Krohn-Rhodes theory.
Algebraic geometry (studying of equations) over wreath products was developed
in [1]. Namely, in [1] it was proved that the wreath product C = A ≀B of a non-
abelian group A and inﬁnite B is not equationally Noetherian, i.e. there exists an
inﬁnite system of equations S over C such that S is not equivalent to any ﬁnite
subsystem. In [11] we obtained the same result using another approach.
In [6] B. Plotkin gave the following list of problems for wreath products.
1. When a wreath product C = A ≀B is equationally Noetherian?
2. When C is qω-compact but not equationally Noetherian?
3. When C is not qω-compact?
First, we note that in the B. Plotkin‘s papers this notion is called logically
Noetherian property (also B.Plotkin used the term “geometrically Noetherian” in-
stead of “equationally Noetherian”). However, in our paper we will use the termi-
nology of [2].
Let us explain the notion of the qω-compactness. The idea of qω-compactness
plays a similar role in universal algebraic geometry as Compactness theorem in
model theory. If any solution P ∈An of a system of equations S(X) also satisﬁes
an equation E(X), then E(X) is said to be an consequence of S(X) over an algebraic
structure (group, semigroup, etc.) A. If S(X) is inﬁnite there arises a question:
is there a ﬁnite subsystem of S(X) with the consequence E(X)? If an algebraic
structure A admits a positive answer for the last question, then A is called qω-
compact (the formal and complete deﬁnition of qω-compactness is given in our paper
1


below). According to the deﬁnition, any equationally Noetherian algebraic structure
is qω-compact (this inclusion explains the statement of the second Plotkin‘s question
above).
There are few examples of qω-compact algebraic structures that are not equa-
tionally Noetherian. In [5] B. Plotkin proved that the direct product of all ﬁnitely
generated groups is qω-compact, but not equationally Noetherian. In [10] there were
studied semigroup equations with constants and deﬁned qω-compact semilattices.
In our paper we study equations over wreath products of semigroups. All stud-
ied equations are coeﬃcient-free, i.e. they have not occurrences of constants, just
variables. For such class of equations we prove two theorems. The following theorem
is devoted to the ﬁrst Plotkin‘s question.
Theorem A. Suppose a semigroup A contains zero and a semigroup B is inﬁnite
cyclic. The wreath product C = A ≀B is equationally Noetherian iﬀA is nilpotent.
Our second theorem deals with the second Plotkin‘s question.
Theorem B. The wreath product C = A≀B of two semigroups A, B is qω-compact
if A contains a zero and B is inﬁnite cyclic.
According to our theorems, there exist many examples of wreath products which
are not equationally Noetherian but qω-compact. Moreover, wreath products have
an interesting property: a semigroup A may be not qω-compact, but nevertheless
the whole wreath product A ≀B is qω-compact.

Preliminaries
Let L = {·} be a semigroup language. Commutative semigroup are often considered
as algebraic structures of the additive language L+ = {+}. The set of all terms of
the language L (L+) is denoted by T (T+). For shortness, such sets are called T -
terms and T+-terms respectively. Clearly, any T -term in variables X = {x1, . . . , xn}
can be written as a product
xi1xi2 . . . xik (1 ≤ij ≤n).
Similarly, any T+-term is equivalent to an expression of the form
α1x1 + α2x2 + . . . + αnxn (αi ∈N = {0, 1, 2, . . .})
over any commutative semigroup.
A semigroup equation (equation, for shortness) is an equality
t(X) = s(X), t, s ∈T .
In other words, any semigroup equation is an atomic formula of the language L.
Similarly, an additive equation is an atomic formula t(X) = s(X), t, s ∈T+ of the
language L+.
Below we sometimes denote equations by capital letters, e.g. E(X). The de-
notation E(X): t(X) = s(X) means that an equation E(X) consists of two parts
t(X) and s(X).
Let us give the main deﬁnitions of algebraic geometry over semigroups (see [2]
for more details). All deﬁnitions below are given for the language L, but one can
easily adapt them for the additive language L+.
A system of semigroup equations (system, for shortness) S(X) is an arbitrary
set of semigroup equations. Notice that we always consider systems with a ﬁnite set

of variables X = {x1, . . . , xn}. The set of all solutions of S(X) in a semigroup A is
denoted by VA(S) ⊆An. Two systems S1, S2 are called equivalent over a semigroup
A if VA(S1) = VA(S2).
A semigroup A is equationally Noetherian if any inﬁnite system S(X) is equiva-
lent to a ﬁnite subsystem S∗(X) ⊆S(X) over A. A semigroup A is qω-compact if
for any inﬁnite system S(X) and an equation E(X) such that

Abstract: We prove that the wreath product C = A ≀B of a semigroup A with zero and an inﬁnite cyclic semigroup B is qω-compact (logically Noetherian). Our result partially solves the Plotkin‘s problem about wreath products in [6].
